projects.title: PaletteBoard
projects.summary: Save photos into colourful mood boards. Every board builds its own colour palette and the whole app takes on its colours.
projects.problem:
Image-saving apps treat a collection as a plain list. Designers and hobbyists collect images for their **mood and colour**, but have no way to see, search or reuse the palette a collection creates.

PaletteBoard reads the main colours of every saved photo and blends them into a palette per board, then builds the experience around it: tinted board pages, colour search and palette export.
highlights: Each board's page is tinted with its own palette, with every accent contrast-checked for readability
Search by text, voice, or photo; browse by 13 colours
A 'Picked for you' feed that learns from what you save
Share boards by read-only link or invite editors and viewers
Google sign-in, installable on Android and iOS
Built with a spec-driven workflow (Spec Kit) and Claude Code

github.description: PaletteBoard: save, organize, and share image collections as color-themed mood boards. Change++ Fall 2026 Coding Challenge.

projects.title: B.A.A. · AI Business Assistant
projects.summary: An AI analytics assistant that improved client response times by 37% and cut manual processing in half.
projects.problem:
Small businesses sit on sales and pricing data but rarely have an analyst to interpret it, so decisions wait on spreadsheets.

As an **ISM Research Scholar** mentored by the **Head AI Engineer at PGA of America**, I built B.A.A. (Business Analysis Assistant), inspired by IBM's Project Ripasso. It lets people upload CSV, Excel or Markdown data and **ask questions in plain English**, then answers with forecasts, recommendations and interactive charts.
projects.role: Full-stack & AI developer · ISM Research Scholar
highlights: Improved client response times by 37% and reduced manual processing by 50%
Natural-language questions over uploaded CSV, Excel and Markdown data
GPT-powered analysis with LangChain orchestration and FAISS semantic search
Automated trend detection, forecasting and strategic recommendations
Interviewed 5+ industry experts; presented to 200+ at the ISM Showcase

github.description: This business assistant essentially transforms raw business data into actionable insights through AI-powered analysis, interactive visualizations, and natural language querying, making it a comprehensive tool for data-driven business decision making.
github.readmeExcerpt:
# Business Analytics Assistant

An AI-powered business analytics platform that combines data analysis, visualization, and natural language processing to provide intelligent business insights.

## Features

- **AI-Powered Analysis**: GPT-4 Turbo integration for intelligent data interpretation
- **Multi-Format Data Support**: Upload CSV, Excel, and Markdown table files
- **Interactive Visualizations**: Dynamic charts and graphs using Plotly
- **Natural Language Queries**: Ask questions in plain English about your data
- **Real-time Processing**: Live data analysis with WebSocket support
- **Vector Database**: FAISS-powered semantic search for contextual understanding

## Technology Stack

- **Backend**: Flask with SocketIO, Pandas & NumPy, OpenAI API, LangChain, FAISS
- **Frontend**: Angular 17 analytics dashboard, React chat interface, Plotly.js

github.readmeExcerpt:
# Campus Connect

A cross-platform mobile app built with Expo and React Native.

## Project structure

- `app/` – main application code (screens, navigation)
- `components/` – reusable UI components
- `constants/` – app-wide constants (colours, etc.)
- `store/` – Zustand state management stores
- `assets/` – images and static assets

Runs on iOS and Android through Expo Go.

projects.problem:
Students miss the clubs and events that would matter to them because campus information is scattered.

As an **AI engineering intern**, I engineered a recommendation engine that **personalizes event and club discovery** from student profiles and event metadata, combining **vector embeddings** with **collaborative filtering**. After launch, engagement rose **62%**, connecting **200+ students** and earning hundreds of sign-ups within weeks.

github.readmeExcerpt:
# Thanuja Rameshbaabu — Developer Portfolio

A fast, accessible portfolio that showcases my GitHub projects to recruiters, with an AI guide
that answers questions about my work and an admin area where I curate everything.

**Design:** "deep-space glass": a dark, airy, futuristic theme with a drifting grid, frosted-glass
cards and a cyan→violet accent, built so the projects are what stands out.

## What visitors get

- **One-page overview** (hero, featured work, all projects, skills, about, contact) with a sticky
  navigation bar that highlights where you are.
- **Featured spotlight + filterable grid**: filter by technology and sort; filtered views are
  shareable links (`/?tech=React`).
- **Case studies** at `/projects/`: cover, quick facts (role, stack, year, status), the
  problem, highlights, screenshot gallery, live demo and code links, share image.
- **Ask AI**: a guide that answers only from portfolio content, cites the projects it used, and
  says plainly when it doesn't know. Streams answers; rate-limited; degrades gracefully.
- **Resume** page with inline PDF, download, and a text version.
- **Contact form** delivered to my inbox, with spam protection that needs no CAPTCHA.
- **Live GitHub stats** strip, a skills map that links to projects, and full keyboard/screen-reader
  support. Lighthouse (mobile): 100 / 100 / 100 / 100.

## What I get (`/admin`)

- **Sign in with GitHub**: only my account is allowed (checked on the server for every request).
- **GitHub sync**: daily and on demand. New repos arrive in *Pending review* and are never public
  until I publish them; deleted/private repos are hidden automatically.
- **Board**: drag projects between *Pending / Published / Hidden*, reorder, ★ feature up to three.
- **Editor**: write each case study, upload screenshots (auto-converted to WebP), see a live
  preview of the public card.
- **Profile & resume**: edit the About section and links, upload a photo, replace the resume PDF
  (its text also teaches the AI guide).

Every save is a commit to this repository, so all content has history and can be undone.

## Tech

Next.js 16 (App Router, React Server Components) · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS v4 · Auth.js v5 ·
Google Gemini (free tier) · Upstash Redis (free) · Resend (free) · Vercel Hobby (free) ·
Vitest · Playwright + axe. **Running cost: $0.**

Built spec-first with [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) and Claude Code:
the [spec](specs/001-developer-portfolio/spec.md), [plan](specs/001-developer-portfolio/plan.md),
[tasks](specs/001-developer-portfolio/tasks.md) and [constitution](.specify/memory/constitution.md)
are in the repo.

## Run locally

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # then set AUTH_SECRET and ADMIN_DEV_LOGIN=1
npm run dev                  # http://localhost:3000
```

Locally everything works without any accounts: content is read from and saved to `content/`,
Ask AI uses offline answers, contact messages are logged, and `/admin` offers development-only
sign-in buttons when `ADMIN_DEV_LOGIN=1`. Generate `AUTH_SECRET` with `npx auth secret`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | Unit tests (Vitest) |
| `npm run test:e2e` | Browser tests on desktop, phone and admin (Playwright, uses installed Chrome; dev server must allow `ADMIN_DEV_LOGIN=1`) |
| `npm run lint` · `npm run typecheck` | ESLint · TypeScript |
| `npm run build` then `npm start -- -p 3001` and `npm run lighthouse` | Production build + mobile Lighthouse gate (fails below 90) |
| `node scripts/screenshots.mjs  [route…]` | Desktop + phone screenshots with headless Chrome |

## Deploy (free)

1. **Push this repo to GitHub** (e.g. `ThanujaR12/portfolio`) and import it in
   [Vercel](https://vercel.com/new). Framework: Next.js; no build settings to change.
2. **GitHub OAuth app** (Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New):
   homepage `https://`, callback `https:///api/auth/callback/github`.
   → `AUTH_GITHUB_ID`, `AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET`.
